INVESTOR BRIEF FOR SEPTEMBER 2026 
Good Afternoon and a warm welcome to all the investors, analysts and other stakeholders 
joining us today for the J&K Bank September 2026 Earnings Call.  
Before we discuss the results, let me introduce my fellow colleagues from Bank’s senior 
management who are accompanying me on this call: 
 
Executive Director, Mr. Sudhir Gupta 
Chief General Managers –Mr. Imtiyaz Ahmad Bhat, Mr. Ashutosh Sareen and Mr. Rajesh 
Malla Tikoo 
Deposit Liability Management Head, Mr. Peer Masood Ahmad 
RAM Banking Head, Mr. Sanjay Gupta 
Corporate Banking Head, Mr. Suresh Kumar Chowdhary 
Impaired Assets Portfolio Management Head, Mr. Tariq Ali 
Chief Risk Officer, Mr. Altaf Hussain Kira 
And our Treasury Head – Mr. Ajay Kohli 
 
The geopolitical uncertainties which persisted in the first quarter of the current financial 
year, have continued to mar the global economy in Q2, following the re-escalation of 
conflict in West Asia, which has driven energy prices sharply higher leading to inflationary 
concerns and increased volatility across financial markets. However, despite these 
persistent geopolitical challenges, the Indian economy has posted a robust growth of 7.8% 
during Q1, driven by domestic consumption and investment. This resilient performance has 
led to a sharp upward revision of India’s GDP growth forecast for 2026-27 by IMF to 7% from 
6.4% earlier. 
 
This resilience in the domestic economy is also reflected in the Bank’s business momentum 
with the Bank’s total business growing by 19.4% YoY, to Rs.3.10 lakh crore as on 30th 
September 2026. The YoY growth across both deposits and advances has been healthy at 
16.3% and 23.7% respectively. The profitability has also improved after a subdued 
performance in the first quarter, with the net profit for this quarter being recorded at 
Rs.546 crores, a sequential jump of almost 29% and a double-digit YoY growth as well. 
 
On the credit side, in alignment with the Bank’s strategic positioning as a retail-focused 
Bank, as emphasized during the Q1 call, the Bank has recorded a sequential growth of 
7.62% in Agricultural Advances and 3.90% in Retail Advances, underscoring the tangible 
progress made in execution. The entire net incremental growth during the quarter has 
been contributed by Retail, Agriculture and MSME Loans (RAM). And this growth has been 
contributed by both JKL and ROI in almost equal proportions to their share in the Bank’s 
outstanding RAM loans. On a YTD basis, more than 60% of the Bank’s net incremental credit 
has been contributed by RAM portfolio.

Within RAM, Bank has registered a YoY growth of around 17% in Agricultural Advances, with 
a double-digit YTD growth for the first half-year. Auto Loans continue to be the best 
performing segment amongst Retail Loans with a YoY growth of over 25%, doing well in 
both JKL and ROI. Housing loans in ROI Division also continue to growth at a healthy pace, 
recording a double-digit YoY growth. 
 
On the deposit front also, the Bank has already achieved a YTD growth of around 7% against 
our guidance of 10% for the financial year with the growth in Term Deposits continuing to 
outpace the growth in CASA in line with the continuing industry trend. However, the gap 
between the growth in Term Deposits and CASA Deposits has narrowed down in this quarter 
as the Bank has been able to record positive CASA inflows during this quarter, after a sharp 
outflow in Q1. As a result, Bank has been able to broadly maintain its CASA Ratio at the 
same level of around 42%, being recorded at 41.97% as on 30th September 2026. 
 
Now, coming to profitability, the Bank has recorded an operating profit of Rs.789 crores 
for the quarter, registering a 27% YoY growth and a 12% QoQ growth. Even on a half-year 
basis, the Bank has recorded a YoY growth of over 15% in Operating Profit, being recorded 
at Rs.1,492 crores for the first-half year of the current fiscal. While the operating income 
for this quarter has grown by over 6% sequentially and 14.5% YoY, the increase in operating 
expenditure continues to be controlled at just 2% QoQ and 6.5% YoY, contributing towards 
improved profitability for the quarter. As a result, Cost to Income Ratio of the Bank for 
this quarter has also moderated substantially on both sequential and YoY basis, being 
recorded at 56.57% for the quarter. 
 
Yield on Advances has remained broadly flat on a sequential basis, being recorded at 8.55% 
for the quarter. However, the increasing contribution of RAM segment to our incremental 
credit portfolio, coupled with the recent repo rate hike is expected to support an 
improvement in the yield from third quarter onwards. The sharp outflow of CASA deposits 
during Q1 continued to weigh on our liability profile, contributing to an increase in the 
Cost of Deposits in this quarter to 4.85%. However, with the surplus liquidity in the banking 
system easing bulk deposit rates combined with the positive CASA inflows in Q2 and the 
reduction in Term Deposit rates by our Bank in this quarter, we expect moderation in the 
Cost of Deposits going forward. Resultantly, the NIM has witnessed compression, being 
recorded at 3.22% for the half year but with expected improvement across both yield and 
cost, the NIM should also improve. 
 
Notwithstanding the prevailing macro-economic uncertainties, the Bank has witnessed a 
notable moderation in slippages during the current fiscal, with Annualized Gross Slippage 
Ratio of just 0.4% for the half-year, as Gross Slippages, in terms of absolute amount, have 
halved compared to the corresponding period last year This reflects the resilience of our 
portfolio and the continued effectiveness of our underwriting and monitoring mechanisms. 
The asset quality metrics also continue to consistently improve reaching decadal best

numbers with GNPA and NNPA as on 30-09-2026 being recorded at 2.23% and 0.51% 
respectively and PCR improving from 90.53% as on 30th June 2026 to 91.76% as on 30th 
September 2026. 
 
Capital Adequacy Ratio has been recorded at 16.57% as on 30th September 2026 with CET 
1 of 13.88%. The Bank is already in the process of raising both equity and debt capital to 
the tune of Rs.1000 crores and Rs.500 crores respectively and will raise the capital at an 
opportune time to support its future growth. 
On the back of improved profitability, RoA has jumped by 20 bps QoQ while RoE has jumped 
by more than 250 bps QoQ and have been recorded at 1.07% and 13.68% respectively for 
the quarter. 
Based on the mid-term review, we have re-assessed our guidance as indicated in the last 
call: 
The revised guidance for FY 2026-27 is 
• Credit growth - 14%+ 
• Deposit growth - 12%+ 
• CASA - 42%+ 
• NIM – will improve from here 
• RoA – 1.20% 
• GNPA – Below 2% 
Thank you for your time today and for giving me a patient hearing. We can start with the 
questions now. 
 
Concluding remarks after Q&A session 
Thank you Avinash and thank you to all the participants for joining in today.  
For any further questions or queries, you can contact our Investor Relations desk.
